measures: refined-metal absorption by bloc (apparent consumption = refined production + imports - exports)

copper.title: Copper

checks.anchor2: USGS US apparent consumption 1.6 Mt + ICSG 15.5 Mt

copper.hs_note: refined copper, unwrought (HS 7403.11/12/13/19) — matches "refinery production" cleanly

lithium.title: Lithium
lithium.hs_note: Li carbonate + hydroxide (HS 2836.91 / 2825.20) — matches lithium-chemical output; no free 2nd country anchor

cobalt.title: Cobalt
cobalt.hs_note: unwrought cobalt / mattes / powders (HS 8105.20) — BUNDLES the DRC hydroxide intermediate China imports to refine, so production + imports double-counts. Fix = national lines (China 81052010 feedstock vs 81052020 refined) — a later tier

nickel.title: Nickel
nickel.hs_note: refined unwrought class-I nickel (HS 7502.10) — MISSES class-II ferronickel/NPI, most of world nickel; the ferronickel HS 7202.60 fix also fails (bundles ~12% NPI with ~35% ferronickel). Needs a lane-specific content model

ree.title: Rare earths
ree.hs_note: REE metals + compounds (HS 2805.30 / 2846.90) — spread across codes, mixes intermediates with refined, and lumps elements. Fix = national 8-digit lines (China 2846.90 -> NdPr/Dy oxide) + stoichiometry — a later tier

copper.title: Copper

anchor2.name: ICSG refined-copper usage (China ~56%)
anchor2.note: REPRODUCIBILITY CHECK, not an anchor: ICSG 'refined copper usage' is itself apparent consumption (refined production + net trade + stock change) — the same sum, same inputs as ours. Landing within 1pp of it confirms our trade parsing and arithmetic are sound; it does NOT independently validate the premise. (ICSG separately estimates China's 'real' usage with an unreported-scrap add-on, a partial bottom-up element, but the headline usage figure is apparent-consumption-based.)

copper.of_what: refined-metal apparent consumption = refined production + imports - exports at the stated HS codes; measures refined-metal ABSORPTION only (excludes direct-melt scrap, which is large in fabricator economies) and assumes zero stock change (materially wrong for China in heavy bonded/SRB stocking years)
copper.hs_note: Four-code test (BACI 2024): adding wire-bars/billets/other-refined 740312/313/319 to cathode 740311 moves every top-15 share by <=0.3pp (fabricators Italy/Germany/Korea/Turkey <=0.1pp; China +1.0pp) and leaves world AC unchanged (they net out globally). So cathode 740311 alone is materially adequate. The published figure keeps the atlas pipeline's RECONCILED/hub-deduped 740311 (higher trade quality than raw BACI); the reconciliation gain (~1pp on China) and the four-code completeness gain roughly cancel.
copper.prod_source: USGS Minerals Yearbook Copper 2022, Table 22 (world refinery production by country)

silicon.title: Silicon

anchor2.name: industry/USGS silicon-metal consumption (China ~55-60%)
anchor2.note: the China anchor is a 5-point RANGE (~55-60%), not a point — almost any plausible build lands inside a 5-point band, so it cannot discriminate a good number from a mediocre one; and USGS is our production input, so there is still no second source with a different upstream. A POINT anchor (a national statistics office publishing silicon consumption, or an independently-built Eurostat PRODCOM EU figure) is what would move silicon toward A.

silicon.of_what: METALLURGICAL silicon metal (HS 280469, <99.99% Si) apparent consumption = production + imports - exports. NOT polysilicon (HS 280461, the solar chain) and NOT semiconductors; silicon metal goes mostly to aluminium alloying, silicones, then polysilicon feedstock. Refined absorption only; 2020 snapshot (USGS MYB silicon lags and the industry has grown since); assumes zero stock change.
silicon.hs_note: 280469 (<99.99% Si) bundles THREE grades in one code — aluminium-alloy grade, chemical/silicone grade, and some upgraded-metallurgical (UMG) silicon — different markets and prices, one HS heading. Fine for a tonnage measure of silicon-metal ABSORPTION (all three are silicon metal being absorbed); NOT usable for any end-use claim, and the reason this can never be an A on HS purity. Ferrosilicon (720221/29) correctly excluded. Trade is hub-exposed (44% of flows, 23% of value via entrepôts; Netherlands a top exporter) — but apparent consumption self-cancels transit, so hubs are annotated, not netted.
silicon.share_note: China's silicon-metal output roughly DOUBLED after 2020, so the 2020 share has very likely moved — read 56% as a 2020 figure, not today's.
silicon.prod_source: USGS Minerals Yearbook Silicon 2020, Table 7 (silicon metal rows only, world production by country)

lead.title: Lead

anchor2.name: ILZSG refined-lead usage (China ~44%)
anchor2.note: REPRODUCIBILITY CHECK, not an anchor: ILZSG 'refined lead usage' is itself apparent consumption (production + net trade) for most countries — the same sum we do. Matching it confirms the arithmetic, not the premise. No free source measures lead use bottom-up.

lead.of_what: refined-lead apparent consumption = refined production + imports - exports (HS 780110, refined unwrought lead). Refined-metal absorption; matched year 2022; excludes lead alloys (780191 Pb-Sb / 780199 other) and direct scrap-melt; assumes zero stock change.
lead.hs_note: 780110 = refined unwrought lead, the clean refined form; lead alloys (780191/780199) excluded. Low hub exposure — top exporters (Korea, Australia, India, China) are producers, not entrepots.
lead.prod_source: USGS Minerals Yearbook Lead (world refinery production by country), 2022

validation: Each metal is graded A/B/C/D on a scorecard (stage-match, HS purity, contained-metal, global closure, multi-anchor), not a single China-share gate. Only A/B are published as measured. Copper is A (clean HS; China 56%=known 56%; anchored to ICSG 15.5 Mt and USGS US 1.6 Mt, two independent sources). Lithium is B (clean, but no free 2nd country anchor). Cobalt/nickel/REE are D: their HS codes bundle intermediates or split forms, so production + imports double-counts (China lands at 223% / 32% / 182% of world).
ceiling: Apparent consumption measures refined-metal absorption, not final demand: it misses metal embodied in imported finished goods. It is bloc-level today; per-country and more metals (lead/zinc/tin/aluminium are the next clean-HS candidates; cobalt/REE need national 8-digit customs lines) are the registry's next phases. Global closure ~cancels under balanced trade, so the real validation is the anchors, not closure.
sources: Production: IEA Critical Minerals Dataset 2024 (CC BY) + Eurostat PRODCOM ds-059358 (EU-27 refined copper) + USGS MCS 2025. Trade: CEPII BACI 2023, refined-form HS. Anchors: ICSG Copper Factbook (free), USGS (free); study-group country usage (INSG/ILZSG/WBMS) is paywalled.
